title: Verbal Adverbs 3: The Perfective -в Form
description: The second verbal adverb type: the perfective form (-в for most verbs, -вшись for reflexives). Take the perfective infinitive, drop -ть, add the suffix.
descriptionRussian: Второй тип деепричастия: совершенный вид на -в (для большинства глаголов) и на -вшись (для возвратных). От инфинитива совершенного вида отсекаем -ть и присоединяем суффикс.
intro: The perfective form is built from the infinitive rather than from a conjugated form, which makes it easier than lesson 1: drop two letters, add one. Reflexive verbs keep their marker and take a longer ending. There is also an older variant you will meet in literature and should recognize without using.
rules: A perfective verbal adverb is formed from the perfective infinitive by dropping -ть and adding -в. Прочитать → прочита- + в → прочитав.
Reflexive perfective verbs (ending in -ться) take -вшись instead, keeping the reflexive marker -сь. Вернуться → вернувшись.
An older suffix -вши (without -сь) appears in literature but is rare in modern Russian. Recognize it; produce -в.
A few perfective verbs (пойти, найти, привезти) form the gerund irregularly. The regular -ть rule covers the rest, which is what you drill here.
examples: Прочитав книгу, она легла на диван. (Having read the book, she lay down on the sofa.)

items.prompt: Recap from L2: in 'Читая книгу, он пил чай', when does the reading happen?
items.promptEnglish: What is the timing of читая relative to пил?
options: Reading happens at the same time as drinking
items.answer: Reading happens at the same time as drinking
items.hint: Recap from lesson 2: imperfective gerunds describe what kind of action?
items.explanation: The imperfective gerund читая carries simultaneous action: the reading and the drinking happen together. Today's lesson introduces the perfective gerund, whose meaning is the mirror image: prior completion.

items.prompt: What is the perfective verbal adverb of прочитать?
items.promptEnglish: Form the perfective gerund of прочитать.
items.hint: Drop -ть from the perfective infinitive. Add the suffix.
items.explanation: Прочитать is perfective. Drop -ть to get прочита-, then add -в: прочитав. Meaning: 'having read.' Читая is the imperfective gerund (the aspect partner, simultaneous-reading meaning); прочитать is the infinitive itself; прочитал is finite past tense.

items.prompt: What is the perfective verbal adverb of увидеть?
items.promptEnglish: Form the perfective gerund of увидеть.
items.hint: From the perfective infinitive, drop -ть and add -в.
items.explanation: Увидеть is perfective. Drop -ть to get увиде-, then add -в: увидев. Meaning: 'having seen.' Видя is the imperfective gerund of видеть (the aspect partner, a different timing); видев mixes aspect membership; увидя is not standard for this verb.

items.prompt: What is the perfective verbal adverb of вернуться?
items.promptEnglish: Form the perfective gerund of вернуться (reflexive).
items.hint: Reflexive perfective verbs take -вшись, keeping the reflexive marker.
items.explanation: Вернуться is reflexive (ends in -ться). The perfective gerund replaces -ться with -вшись: верну- + вшись = вернувшись (having returned). Возвращаясь is the imperfective gerund of возвращаться (the aspect partner); вернуть is the non-reflexive infinitive (a different verb); вернувши is the older non-reflexive suffix and would also drop the reflexive marker.

items.promptEnglish: Pick the perfective verbal adverb of сказать.
items.hint: Сказать is the perfective infinitive. Apply the formation rule.
items.explanation: Сказав is the perfective gerund of сказать (drop -ть, add -в). Meaning: 'having said.' Говоря is the imperfective gerund of говорить (the aspect partner) and means 'speaking,' a simultaneous reading; сказать is the infinitive; сказал is the finite past.

items.promptEnglish: Having finished work, Anton went home.
items.hint: The work was finished BEFORE Anton went home. Which form expresses prior completion?
items.explanation: Закончив is the perfective gerund of закончить (drop -ть, add -в). It signals that the work was completed before the home-going. Заканчивая is the imperfective gerund and would mean 'while finishing,' a simultaneous reading; закончить is the infinitive; закончил is the finite past.

fillInBlank.grammarFocus: The perfective verbal adverb expresses an action completed before the main verb.
hints: The hearing happens first; then he starts dancing. Which form expresses a prior completed action?
explanations: Услышав is the perfective gerund of услышать (drop -ть, add -в). It marks the hearing as completed before the dancing began. Слушая is the imperfective gerund ('while listening'); услышать is the infinitive; услышал is finite past tense.

errorCorrection.sentence: Умывший холодной водой, Антон окончательно проснулся.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: Having washed his face with cold water, Anton finally woke up.
errorCorrection.explanation: Умыться is a reflexive perfective verb, so its gerund keeps the reflexive marker and ends in -вшись: умывшись ('having washed up'). Умывший is the active past participle of the transitive умыть and would need an object. Умыв would also demand an object (умыв ребёнка).

errorCorrection.translationEnglish: Having bought the groceries, Lena went home.
errorCorrection.explanation: Купить is perfective, so the gerund marks a prior completed action: drop -ть from the infinitive and add -в → купив ('having bought'). Купия wrongly uses the imperfective -я suffix, which clashes with a perfective stem. Купивши is archaic and купивший a participle.

errorCorrection.translationEnglish: Having learned the news, Lena called her mom.
errorCorrection.explanation: The perfective gerund of узнать is узнав ('having learned'), made by dropping -ть and adding -в; it compresses a completed prior action before the main verb. Узнавший is the active past participle ('the one who learned'), which agrees with a noun like an adjective and cannot stand at the head of a gerund clause; learners reach for it because both forms start узнав-. Узная uses the imperfective -я suffix, wrong for a perfective verb, and узнавши is the dated -вши variant. The news is learned before the call, so узнав is the right form.

minimalPairs.context: _____ книгу, она положила её на стол.
minimalPairs.contextEnglish: Having read the book, she put it on the table.
minimalPairs.explanation: The reading is finished, then she puts the book down. The two actions are sequential, calling for the perfective Прочитав. Читая would mean she puts the book down WHILE reading it, which the sentence does not support.

minimalPairs.contextEnglish: Having finished work, Anton went to sleep.
minimalPairs.explanation: Finishing the work is a completed prior action; sleep comes after. The perfective Закончив fits. Заканчивая ('while finishing') would imply Anton fell asleep mid-work, a different reading.

categorySorting.instruction: Sort each gerund by its aspect.

reviewVocab.definition: perfective verbal adverb (-в / -вшись; expresses an action completed before the main verb)
reviewVocab.example: Прочитав, услышав, узнав — все это совершенные деепричастия.

reviewVocab.definition: infinitive (the dictionary form of the verb; the perfective gerund is built from it by dropping -ть and adding the suffix)
reflexive verb (one ending in -ться); its perfective gerund takes -вшись to keep the reflexive marker -сь
before (the timing relation in the perfective gerund's reading: the secondary action happens before the main one)
reviewVocab.example: Прочитав книгу, она лежала на диване — чтение до того, как она легла.
